title: Letrozole for PCOS infertility: suppresses ovarian estradiol (aromatase inhibition)
vignette: A 30-year-old nulligravid woman and her 31-year-old husband come to the office for an infertility evaluation. They have been unable to conceive despite 2 years of unprotected intercourse. The patient has had irregular periods since menarche, ranging between 30 and 70 days each cycle. Her BMI is 34 kg/m2. Examination shows a small, anteverted uterus and bilateral enlarged ovaries. A urine pregnancy test is negative. The patient is prescribed letrozole for ovulation induction therapy. This medication is most likely to help this patient through which of the following mechanisms?

clues.text: irregular periods since menarche, ranging between 30 and 70 days
clues.note: Chronic oligomenorrhea (irregular, infrequent cycles) with obesity and enlarged ovaries suggests polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) with anovulation.
Enlarged (often polycystic) ovaries support PCOS - a common cause of anovulatory infertility.
Letrozole is an AROMATASE INHIBITOR used for ovulation induction; it blocks conversion of androgens to estrogen, lowering estradiol.

whatMatters: In PCOS, high ovarian estrogen suppresses FSH/LH and prevents ovulation. LETROZOLE is an AROMATASE INHIBITOR that blocks androgen-to-estrogen conversion, SUPPRESSING OVARIAN ESTRADIOL production. The resulting drop in estrogen releases the pituitary to secrete more FSH/LH, stimulating follicle growth and ovulation. Answer E.
strategy: Know letrozole's mechanism: aromatase inhibition -> less estrogen -> loss of estrogen's negative feedback -> increased FSH/LH -> ovulation. The listed mechanism is 'suppression of ovarian estradiol production.' Reject clomiphene's mechanism (estrogen-RECEPTOR blockade/depletion at the hypothalamus - a different drug), dopamine-receptor activation (bromocriptine for hyperprolactinemia), endometrial proliferation (unopposed estrogen effect, not ovulation induction), and continuous GnRH agonism (leuprolide - suppresses gonadotropins).

eliminations.label: Pituitary dopamine receptor activation - bromocriptine
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a dopamine agonist mechanism (bromocriptine/cabergoline) that lowers prolactin. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that treats hyperprolactinemia-related infertility, not PCOS anovulation with letrozole. ✅ Correct if: infertility from a prolactinoma.

eliminations.label: Depletion of hypothalamic estrogen receptors - clomiphene (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the mechanism of CLOMIPHENE, a selective estrogen receptor modulator that binds/depletes hypothalamic estrogen receptors, blocking negative feedback -> more FSH/LH. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that is a different drug; LETROZOLE instead INHIBITS AROMATASE to lower estradiol. ✅ Correct if: the drug were clomiphene.

eliminations.label: Increased endometrial proliferation - unopposed estrogen
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: estrogen-driven endometrial growth (a risk of unopposed estrogen/tamoxifen). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: letrozole LOWERS estrogen and does not act by proliferating endometrium. ✅ Correct if: asking about unopposed-estrogen endometrial hyperplasia.

eliminations.label: Inhibition of hypothalamic gonadotropin secretion - continuous GnRH agonist
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: continuous GnRH agonism (leuprolide) downregulates GnRH receptors, DECREASING FSH/LH. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that SUPPRESSES ovulation (used to create a menopause-like state), the opposite of ovulation induction. ✅ Correct if: continuous leuprolide for downregulation.

reasoning: PCOS causes anovulatory infertility, partly from high ovarian estrogen suppressing FSH/LH
Letrozole inhibits aromatase, blocking androgen-to-estrogen conversion
This suppresses ovarian estradiol -> less negative feedback -> more FSH/LH -> follicle growth and ovulation
-> suppression of ovarian estradiol production; answer E
mechanism: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) commonly causes anovulatory infertility; increased ovarian production of estrogen (estradiol) exerts negative feedback that suppresses pituitary FSH/LH and prevents normal follicle selection/ovulation. LETROZOLE is an AROMATASE INHIBITOR: aromatase (in ovarian granulosa cells and peripheral adipose tissue) converts androgens to estrogens, so blocking it SUPPRESSES OVARIAN ESTRADIOL (and peripheral estrone) production. The fall in estrogen removes negative feedback on the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, so the pituitary releases MORE FSH (and LH), which stimulates follicular development and triggers ovulation. Letrozole has largely replaced clomiphene for PCOS ovulation induction (higher live-birth rates, less multiple-gestation/antiestrogenic endometrial effect). Note the contrast: CLOMIPHENE works differently - as a selective estrogen receptor modulator that binds and 'depletes' hypothalamic estrogen receptors to block feedback. The other options are mechanisms of bromocriptine (dopamine agonist), unopposed estrogen (endometrial proliferation), and continuous GnRH agonists (gonadotropin suppression).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Repro/Pharm > letrozole = aromatase inhibitor -> ↓estradiol -> ↑FSH/LH -> ovulation (PCOS); clomiphene = SERM (estrogen-receptor blockade at hypothalamus); both induce ovulation by different mechanisms.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Letrozole lowers estrogen (aromatase inhibition) -> pituitary releases more FSH/LH -> ovulation.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on aromatase, estradiol, negative feedback, FSH/LH, or clomiphene vs letrozole? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Clomiphene (estrogen-receptor depletion) is a DIFFERENT drug; bromocriptine (dopamine), leuprolide (GnRH downregulation), and endometrial proliferation don't fit letrozole.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: letrozole (aromatase inhibitor) -> ↓estrogen -> ↑FSH -> ovulation in PCOS; clomiphene = SERM at hypothalamus.

keywords.back: SERM - blocks/depletes hypothalamic estrogen receptors (removes feedback)
Elevated estrogen/androgens disrupt FSH/LH and follicle selection

firstAid.detail: Repro > anovulation; letrozole first-line ovulation induction.

memoryHook: Letrozole starves the ovary of estrogen (blocks aromatase); the pituitary, no longer told to hush, pumps out FSH and pops a follicle - ovulation in PCOS.
